purpose: Add eight source-exact John Newton hymn and devotional excerpts for worship, prayer, faith, and Christian growth.

defaults.author: John Newton
defaults.rightsBasis: This 1808 E. Duyckinck edition is public domain; every excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should be checked against the page scan before publication.

entries.title: The promise cannot come too late
entries.text: The promise may be long delay'd, But cannot come too late.
entries.slideText: The promise may be long delay'd, But cannot come too late.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed hymn couplet in a sermon about patiently trusting God's promises.
entries.reviewNote: This is poetry, not Scripture. Explain the cited promises in their KJV context and avoid attaching a private timetable to them.

entries.title: The Lord will provide
entries.text: Yet one thing secures us, Whatever betide, The scripture assures us, The Lord will provide,
entries.slideText: Yet one thing secures us, Whatever betide, The scripture assures us, The Lord will provide,
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed hymn stanza before teaching God's wise and sufficient provision.
entries.reviewNote: Do not present provision as a promise of ease or wealth. Define need and contentment from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Hope built upon His word
entries.text: The hope that's built upon his word, Can ne'er be overthrown.
entries.slideText: The hope that's built upon his word, Can ne'er be overthrown.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed hymn excerpt connecting Christian perseverance with confidence in God's word.
entries.reviewNote: The line is an excerpt from a stanza. Keep its visible attribution and establish assurance directly from the cited KJV texts.

entries.title: A thankful song
entries.text: His praises should employ each tongue, And ev'ry heart enflame !
entries.slideText: His praises should employ each tongue, And ev'ry heart enflame !
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed call to congregational praise or a transition into a message about Christian singing.
entries.reviewNote: This is devotional poetry. Teach the purpose and content of Christian song from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Trust less to our own strength
entries.text: We learn to tread more warily, to trust less to our own strength, to have lower thoughts of ourselves, and higher thoughts of Him ;
entries.slideText: We learn to tread more warily, to trust less to our own strength
entries.sourceTitle: Cardiphonia: Or, The Utterance of the Heart
entries.rightsBasis: This 1911 Religious Tract Society edition is public domain; the excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should be checked against the page scan before publication.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed observation about humility and dependence on the Lord in Christian growth.
entries.reviewNote: The slide uses an exact shortened clause from the full excerpt. Keep the attribution visible and ground the application in the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Here we are to walk by faith
entries.text: Here we are to walk by faith, to be exercised and tried ; by and by we shall be crowned, and the desires He has given shall be abundantly satisfied.
entries.slideText: Here we are to walk by faith, to be exercised and tried ; by and by we shall be crowned
entries.sourceTitle: Cardiphonia: Or, The Utterance of the Heart
entries.rightsBasis: This 1911 Religious Tract Society edition is public domain; the excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should be checked against the page scan before publication.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed devotional line when teaching faithfulness through testing.
entries.reviewNote: Do not imply that every desire will be granted as imagined. Let the cited KJV passages define faith, trial, and maturity.

entries.title: Prayer is his breath
entries.text: Prayer is his breath, the word of God his food, and the ordinances more precious to him than the light of the sun.
entries.slideText: Prayer is his breath, the word of God his food
entries.sourceTitle: Cardiphonia: Or, The Utterance of the Heart
entries.rightsBasis: This 1911 Religious Tract Society edition is public domain; the excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should be checked against the page scan before publication.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed devotional image for the believer's continual need of prayer and Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: The metaphors are Newton's, not Scripture. Ground the application in the cited KJV texts and do not turn devotional habits into a measure of salvation.

entries.title: Communion with God
entries.text: Though he knows that communion with God is his highest privilege, he too seldom finds it so ;
entries.slideText: communion with God is his highest privilege
entries.sourceTitle: Cardiphonia: Or, The Utterance of the Heart
entries.rightsBasis: This 1911 Religious Tract Society edition is public domain; the excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should be checked against the page scan before publication.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed self-examination prompt about valuing fellowship with God.
entries.reviewNote: The slide extracts a clause from Newton's larger sentence. Keep the attribution visible and teach access to God through Christ from the cited KJV texts.
